overall: Los Angeles is locked in a classic June Gloom marine-layer pattern this morning, with temperatures remarkably flat at 62–63°F from midnight through 8:30 AM ET — essentially zero overnight or early-morning warming. Patchy fog and mostly cloudy skies are suppressing any surface heating, with light southwest onshore flow (under 5 mph) reinforcing the cool, moist boundary layer (dewpoint ~57°F). The day should eventually warm once the fog burns off around 11 AM local time, but cloud cover will limit the afternoon peak.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models are in good agreement, clustering tightly between 67.0°F (NBM) and 69.5°F (HRRR), with ECMWF at 68.2°F — a spread of only 2.5°F. The NWS narrative high of ~69°F aligns well with this model consensus. All three models peg the peak hour at 16–17h ET (1–2 PM PT), consistent with a late-afternoon warming window after fog clears. The intraday observation-driven distribution shows a wide, flatter spread (peaking around 74–77°F) that appears somewhat elevated relative to the tighter NWP guidance, likely reflecting uncertainty from the very flat early-morning obs baseline.
max_temp_prediction: The most likely daily high is in the 67–69°F range, broadly consistent with all three NWP models and the NWS forecast. The persistent marine layer, flat overnight temperatures, and mostly cloudy afternoon skies argue against the upper tail of the intraday distribution; a run above 72°F would require an unexpectedly strong and early fog clearance plus sustained solar heating. Confidence is moderate-to-high that the max lands in the 67–70°F corridor, with the center of gravity near 68°F. Key risk to the upside is fog clearing earlier than forecast; downside risk is clouds persisting through the afternoon and capping the high near 65–66°F.
